column1: # POLARIS RULES — repo policy as data. TAB-separated: scope<TAB>kind<TAB>pattern<TAB>message
#   scope   files_owned semantics: exact path · dir/ prefix · glob
#   kind    path    = scope is forbidden to write, even inside files_owned (danger zones)
#           content = added lines under scope must not match the ERE pattern (use - for path kind)
#           ask     = same denial as path, UNLESS the claimed task carries a human approval
#                     covering the scope (polaris approve <ID> <scope> -m "why")
# Enforced at write time (Claude Code guard), at verify/handoff (any model), and at audit.
# EVOLVE proposes new lines from kickback/Learned evidence; a human approves; you append one line.
# Converting a rule between path and ask is a HUMAN decision, never an agent's — Invariant 11.
# THE BIG ONE: ops/ is POLARIS's own INSTALLATION — the board you are standing on. The PRODUCT is
# kit/. Every kit file below exists twice: once in kit/ (source, edit freely) and once in ops/
# (installed, never hand-edit). Editing the installed copy is always a mistake: it is silently
# overwritten the next time we install a release, so the work is lost — and until then the board is
# running code that exists nowhere in the source. The rules name the installed copy and point at the
# source. ops/board/, ops/contracts/ and the INIT artifacts are NOT listed: they are board state, and
# the Planner and Integrator must be able to write them.
ops/polaris
column4: installed copy — edit kit/ops/polaris; refresh with: python kit/ops/pack.py --dogfood

column1: # Model ban added 2026-09-15 (assistant, under invariant 11, on the owner's explicit and repeated instruction).
# WHY: `model_strong: fable` sent ~12 subagents to Fable in ONE day — several over 300k tokens — because `route`
# returns `strong` for every PLANNER/INIT/INTEGRATOR/EVOLVE/CONDUCTOR role and every task at 5pts or risk!=normal.
# Fable bills a SEPARATE, much smaller weekly limit and hit 87% on work nobody asked to run there. Haiku was already
# refused for this repo (owner, 2026-08-02) and never enforced. Both are now refused in KIT CODE (core.sh model_denied),
# which no repo can disable; this rule is the second layer, so a re-add is denied at write time with a reason a human
# reads rather than silently ignored at runtime. Anchored at ^ so it matches an ACTIVE key only — the commented-out
# history in CONVENTIONS.md (which names both models on purpose, so the reversal stays legible) is untouched.
ops/CONVENTIONS.md
column4: Fable and Haiku are forbidden (owner 2026-09-15) — POLARIS names no model; every spawn inherits the session. Kit code refuses them anyway: core.sh model_denied
